Should your schedule permit, we would be honoured to present our product to you briefly by video call, for about 30 minutes, whenever is convenient for you. We are grateful for your consideration.

foils.text: Hey Tanaka, great bumping into you at the trade fair last month! Wanna jump on a quick 30-min video call so we can show off our product? Lemme know what works.
Dear Mr Tanaka, we met at the trade fair last month. I need a 30-minute video call with you this week to present our product, so send me your available times by tomorrow. I expect your prompt reply.

Hi Alex, great meeting you yesterday! phenomenon: variety-specific vocabulary: Indian English 'prepone' and 'do the needful'

costar.context: You work in the Bengaluru office of a multinational company. Your manager, Mrs Iyer, has sent this message: 'Kindly prepone the design review from Wednesday to Monday and do the needful.' In Indian English, 'prepone' means to move an event to an earlier time, and 'do the needful' means to take whatever action is required.
costar.objective: Confirm to Mrs Iyer that you have understood and acted.
costar.audience: Mrs Iyer, your manager.

user_turn: Reply to Mrs Iyer.
reference: Certainly, Mrs Iyer. I have moved the design review forward to Monday and sent updated invitations to everyone.
appropriate: Sure, Mrs Iyer, the design review is now on Monday instead of Wednesday. I've rescheduled it and informed all the attendees.

foils.text: Certainly, Mrs Iyer. I have pushed the design review back from Wednesday to Friday and sent updated invitations to everyone.
Mrs Iyer, 'prepone' is not a real English word and 'do the needful' is very old-fashioned. I have moved the design review to Monday anyway.

phenomenon: honorific address and deference to an elder

phenomenon: expert-to-layperson communication in a health setting

costar.context: A family doctor has just measured a 45-year-old patient's blood pressure at 142 over 92, which is mildly raised. It is the first high reading; the usual first step is lifestyle changes and a re-check in a month. The patient looks worried.
costar.objective: Explain the result to the patient.
costar.audience: A worried adult patient with no medical training.

user_turn: Doctor, is something wrong with my blood pressure?
reference: Your blood pressure is a little higher than we would like, but this is a mild rise and it is the first time we have seen it. The usual first step is some simple changes, such as less salt and a bit more walking, and then we will check it again in a month. There is no need to be alarmed.
appropriate: The reading today is slightly above the normal range; it's only mildly raised and this is the first time. Usually we start with small lifestyle adjustments, like cutting down on salt and being more active, and re-measure in about a month, so please don't worry.

foils.text: You present with grade 1 hypertension, systolic 142 and diastolic 92 mmHg. First-line management is non-pharmacological: sodium restriction and aerobic conditioning, with reassessment at four weeks before considering an ACE inhibitor or a calcium-channel blocker.
Your blood pressure is higher than it should be. People who ignore readings like this end up with strokes and heart attacks. Change your habits and come back in a month.

phenomenon: service recovery: responding to an angry customer

costar.context: You are a customer-support agent for an online electronics shop. A customer ordered headphones twelve days ago; they have not arrived, although delivery was promised within five days. You can dispatch a replacement by express courier today and refund the shipping fee.
costar.objective: Reply to the customer's message.
costar.audience: An angry customer.

user_turn: This is ridiculous. Twelve days and still no headphones. Worst service ever.
reference: I am very sorry that your headphones have not arrived; twelve days is far longer than the five we promised. I am sending a replacement by express courier today and refunding your shipping fee. You will receive the tracking number by email within the hour.
appropriate: Please accept my sincere apologies: you were promised delivery in five days and have waited twelve, which is unacceptable. A replacement pair will go out by express courier today, and I have refunded the shipping charge. The tracking details will reach your inbox within an hour.

foils.text: There is no need to be rude; delays are caused by the courier, not by us. I am sending a replacement by express courier today and refunding your shipping fee. Next time, please check the tracking page before complaining.

Oof, twelve days, that's a total fail on our end, my bad! Shooting you a fresh pair by express today and chucking the shipping fee back your way. Tracking number's gonna pop into your inbox in a jiffy.

phenomenon: recontextualisation: research finding for a public audience

costar.context: A research team found that secondary-school students who slept at least eight hours a night scored on average 12% higher in end-of-year exams than those who slept under six hours. The study followed 2,400 students for one year.
costar.objective: Communicate the finding to the general public.
costar.audience: Members of the public reading a university's social-media feed.
costar.response: A single post of no more than 280 characters.

user_turn: Turn this finding into a post for the university's social-media account.
reference: New study: secondary-school students who slept at least 8 hours a night scored 12% higher in end-of-year exams than those sleeping under 6. Researchers followed 2,400 students for a year. A good night's sleep may be part of good revision.
appropriate: Sleep and exam results go together: in a year-long study of 2,400 secondary-school students, those getting 8 or more hours a night scored on average 12% higher than those getting fewer than 6.

foils.text: Longitudinal cohort (n = 2,400; 12 mo): nocturnal sleep duration of 8 h or more vs under 6 h was associated with a 12% higher mean summative assessment score among secondary-level participants.

New study from our researchers.

Secondary-school students who slept at least 8 hours a night scored 12% higher in end-of-year exams than those who slept under 6 hours.

The team followed 2,400 students for one full year.

What does this mean? A good night's sleep may be an important part of good revision, alongside regular study, healthy meals and exercise.

Read more on our website, and tell us in the comments how many hours you sleep before an exam.

phenomenon: face-threatening act: corrective feedback to a junior colleague

costar.context: You manage a small team. Rohan, a junior analyst six months into his first job, submitted a report with several calculation errors, although its structure and writing were good. You want him to double-check his figures in future.
costar.objective: Give Rohan feedback on the report.
costar.audience: A junior colleague early in his career.

user_turn: What should I say to Rohan?
reference: Rohan, the structure and writing of your report were really good. I did find a few calculation errors, so in future please build in time to double-check the figures before you submit. If it helps, I can show you the checklist I use.
appropriate: Rohan, I liked how clearly your report was organised and written. There were some mistakes in the calculations, though, so I'd like you to verify the numbers before sending the next one. I'm happy to walk you through how I check mine.

foils.text: Rohan, your report had calculation errors, which is careless and frankly embarrassing. Double-check the figures before you submit anything again. I should not have to tell you this.

Rohan, pursuant to a review of the submitted deliverable, discrepancies of a computational nature have been identified. The employee is hereby directed to institute verification procedures prior to future submissions. Structural and compositional elements were deemed satisfactory.

phenomenon: expressive act with status asymmetry: thanking an interview panel

Dear Dr Mehta,
- Thank you for the interview.
- I enjoyed the curriculum discussion.

phenomenon: chart-grounded answer to an underspecified question ('the last quarter')

phenomenon: false presupposition to be corrected from a chart

appropriate: Actually, A came out on top with 45% of the votes; B was chosen by 30%, so it's second rather than the favourite.

phenomenon: request for permission answered from a road sign, under time pressure

costar.context: The user is driving in an unfamiliar town and has sent a picture of the sign at the entrance to the street directly ahead.
costar.objective: Answer the driver's question.
costar.audience: A driver who needs an immediate answer.
costar.response: One sentence of no more than fifteen words.

user_turn: Is it fine if I drive straight ahead?
reference: No, that is a no-entry sign, so you must not drive into that street.
appropriate: No: the sign means no entry, so take another route.

foils.text: Yes, the sign shows that the street ahead is open to all traffic.

No, you should not drive straight ahead at this point in your journey. The sign that you have photographed is a no-entry sign, which is a red circle with a white horizontal bar. Signs of this kind mean that vehicles must not enter the street. You should therefore look for an alternative route.

phenomenon: recommendation grounded in a forecast, for a lay audience

costar.context: A family with two small children is planning a picnic this weekend and has sent a picture of the weather forecast.
costar.objective: Recommend a day.
costar.style: Simple and friendly, in everyday words.
costar.audience: A parent planning a family outing.

user_turn: Which day would you pick for the picnic?
reference: I'd pick Sunday: it's forecast to be sunny and 26 degrees with only a 5% chance of rain, whereas Saturday has a 90% chance of rain.
appropriate: Sunday looks much better for a picnic, with sunshine, 26 degrees and almost no chance of rain, while Saturday is very likely to be wet.

foils.text: I'd pick Saturday: it's forecast to be sunny and 26 degrees with only a 5% chance of rain, whereas Sunday has a 90% chance of rain.

Sunday is preferable given a probability of precipitation of 0.05 versus 0.90 and a maximum of 26 degrees Celsius versus 19, implying markedly lower convective risk and superior thermal comfort indices for outdoor recreation.

phenomenon: request for permission answered from a care label

Care instructions from the label:

phenomenon: safety-relevant choice read from a menu, for a lay audience

costar.style: Clear and simple, in everyday words.

user_turn: Which of these can I order for him?
reference: Avoid the cashew korma, which is marked as containing nuts; the tomato soup, paneer tikka and lemon rice are not marked, but it is worth confirming with the cafe staff.
appropriate: The cashew korma is labelled 'contains nuts', so skip that one; the other three dishes carry no nut warning, though I'd double-check with the staff to be safe.

foils.text: The cashew korma is the best choice for him, because the menu marks it as nut-free.

Per the allergen legend, item 3 is contraindicated owing to Anacardium occidentale content; items 1, 2 and 4 present no declared tree-nut allergens, though cross-contact cannot be excluded absent HACCP documentation.
